boundary_decision.status: accepted as an authorization process case, not the permission-bearing grant
boundary_decision.rationale: The legacy specification and registry purpose define application-to-decision processing. The case owns submissions, assessments, consultations, decisions and follow-on administrative actions, while the actual grant, reusable service, law, criteria, evidence artifacts, payments, inspections, enforcement and appeals remain external masters.

decisions.rationale: A favorable decision references a separately mastered right or attestation; process completion, a permit number and current grant validity cannot be inferred from one another.
Permit, licence, approval, registration, exemption and certificate may differ by sector and legal system and are not universal synonyms.

decisions.disposition: accepted as external masters with case-specific use
decisions.rationale: The case records submission, supported claim, verification and assessment, while reusable criteria and source evidence artifacts retain independent identity and privacy policy.
Automated checks and recommendations may inform a result but cannot invent competence, due process, reasons or legal effect.
Renewal, variation, transfer, suspension, revocation, annulment, surrender and reinstatement record authority and effect without mutating the external grant by inference.

decisions.disposition: accepted as separate case and grant axes
decisions.rationale: Submission, review, decision, notification and closure state is not external grant state; decision, effect, observation and knowledge times remain distinct.
A case projection may show a decision and reference, but current authorization validity must resolve the authoritative grant, scope, jurisdiction and freshness.
CPSV-AP, CCCEV, LegalRuleML and UN/CEFACT FLAP address different service, evidence, legal and sector concerns, so mappings disclose version and loss.
